clues.text: This city sits in the southwest of a country in Africa. It stands on the Chari River, not far from Lake Chad.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside the southwest of Chad on a river near a large lake

source.quote: N'Djamena is situated on the Chari River in the southwestern part of Chad, near Lake Chad.

clues.text: This place has a hot, dry climate with one clear dry season each year. The river gives water for farms and homes, but the flat land around it stays dry.
clues.narrowing: narrows to hot, dry parts of the region with a clear dry season

source.quote: The city lies within a semi-arid region characterized by a hot climate with a distinct dry season. Its location on the river provides vital water resources for agriculture and daily life, although the surrounding landscape is largely flat and arid.

clues.text: French rulers founded this city in 1910 when they held this part of Africa. It got a new local name in 1975 to show its own roots.
clues.narrowing: narrows to French-founded cities in central Africa from 1910

source.quote: Originally called Fort-Lamy, it was founded in 1910 by the French during their colonization of Central Africa. The city was renamed N'Djamena in 1975, reflecting its local Chadian heritage.

clues.text: Two big rivers meet here, and a town in the next country sits just across the water. This port town is a key crossroads for trade in the whole region.
clues.narrowing: narrows to the port where two rivers meet on the border with Cameroon

source.quote: It is a port city located at the confluence of the Logone River with the Chari River, forming a transborder agglomeration with the city of Kousséri (in Cameroon), capital of the Department of Logone-et-Chari, which is on the west bank of both rivers.

clues.text: This is Chad's capital, its seat of rule. It is the biggest city in the whole land too.
